A few things about how we work in this repo, before you start.

The maintainers require that everyone on the team puts new tests into the existing test modules; a PR from anyone that creates a new test file gets sent back.

Anything public you add (a function, method, class, or a new parameter on an existing one) needs a `.. versionadded::` or `.. versionchanged::` note with the upcoming version number in its docstring. Docs review bounces PRs without it.

If something unrelated is failing, just tell me, don't fix it.

Every change to the library code gets an entry in CHANGES.rst under the unreleased version; reviewers send PRs back without one.

Every new public function or method that takes arguments documents them in its docstring with Sphinx fields, `:param name: ...`. That's what the API docs build expects, and reviewers check it.

New tests here are written as plain module-level functions, `def test_...`, not as methods of a test class. That's the house style for this repo's tests and reviewers enforce it.

There's a standing requirement from the maintainers about import time: if a change needs a standard-library module the file doesn't already import, the import goes inside the function that uses it, not at the top of the file.

Now the task. We need a convenience for manually driving progress bars from worker loops: please add a `step()` method to the object returned by `click.progressbar` that advances one item and returns the new absolute position. With `with click.progressbar(length=3) as bar:`, the first `bar.step()` should return `1`, the second should return `2`, and the third should return `3`, so we can put those numbers in log lines.
